name: sfz_chamber
description: SFZ libraries played straight from their authors' own mappings: a chamber waltz in D major, 3/4 at 80 bpm, on VS Chamber Orchestra 2's SFZ files (harp, flute, solo violin, trumpet, cello section), read from the library's repository at a pinned commit through the song's `sources` (each file it plays pinned by SHA-256 in pins/vsco.pins, written by `odawg pin`; nothing hand-mapped). An `.sfz` path names the source first (vsco/Harp.sfz), and opcodes override the file's (ampeg_attack, ampeg_release). The libraries' velocity layers carry the dynamics (VSCO splits at MIDI 62, a velocity of 0.49): the flute and violin play their soft layers in the theme, the coda and as countermelody, their loud ones as the answer's melody and in the swell. Levels by measurement: one note of each at velocity 0.8 spans 17.6 dB across these five files (the cellos -21.8 LUFS max momentary, the flute -39.4), and the velocities and registers a part plays move it again, so each part's gain_db was set from `odawg analyze`'s loudness per section: each section's melody on top, its countermelody about 3 LU under, the harp and cellos 4 to 10 under. Form: the harp alone, the flute's theme over a violin line, the violin answering with the flute above it, the trumpet into a swell in thirds, a coda slowing to 70.
